analyst_view.overall: Borac (21st, 3 pts) host Atalanta (16th, 4 pts) in a game both need for a top-24 place; Borac arrive on three straight wins in all competitions and are unbeaten at home in Europe since qualifying began, while their only league-phase win came against KuPS. Atalanta drew 4-4 with Inter on Sunday and lost first-choice keeper Marco Carnesecchi (torn meniscus), so Sportiello starts; the numbers already count that (+6% to Borac's goals). Centre-backs Hien and Kossounou are also expected to miss out, as they did recently, and with Lecce next Sarri is expected to rotate: one preview has Scamacca, Samardzic, Sulemana and Rowe starting and De Ketelaere on the bench. Borac only have Cipetic to be assessed. Belgian referee Nathan Verboomen is named; the numbers have no usable record for him.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, with Atalanta scoring about 2, already lifted for Borac's recent scoring and for Carnesecchi's absence (+6%). Atalanta are without Hien and Kossounou at the back, but they were missing in recent games too, so the momentum already carries that, and a rotated attack (Scamacca rather than Krstovic, De Ketelaere rested) pulls the other way, so I stay at about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, about 6 for Atalanta. Atalanta should have most of the ball and Borac have been conceding plenty of corners, which the numbers already add through recent form (+7% for Atalanta). A rotated front line still plays the same wide game under Sarri, so I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, and they already raise Borac's share by about 19% for their recent card count. A home side chasing a stronger team tends to foul more, but that is what the numbers already show, and the named referee, Nathan Verboomen, has too little record at this level to point either way, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.0 shots, 19 of them Atalanta's, already lifted for both sides' recent volume. I lean slightly lower: after a draining 4-4 with Inter and with Lecce next, Sarri is expected to rotate and may manage the game rather than chase it, which the numbers can't see. A mild -3% gives about 31.0 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target, already raised for both sides' recent accuracy. A stand-in keeper and Borac's open defence both point to chances at each end, which the numbers already count, while a rotated Atalanta attack may be a little less sharp; those roughly cancel, so I stay at about 10.7.
